title: Proof ledger for asynchronous structured-output metering (embeddings/rerank/fncall)
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Non-chat endpoints that run multi-stage pipelines (embedding fanouts, rerank, and structured function-calls) produce complex billing signals: partial tool executions, truncated structured responses, retries, and speculative prefetches make per-item charging ambiguous. Current heuristics occasionally double-charge or fail to refund prefetched items when downstream cancellation occurs. Goal: design and implement a minimal, auditable proof ledger that records canonical events for each request/item so final billing can deterministically reconcile provisional credits and emit a single committed charge per logical operation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Each non-chat multi-stage request emits a compact per-item event ledger that survives retries and deduplication: (request_id, item_id, event_type, event_hash, canonical_timestamp).
2) Billing system uses 'commit' events to finalize charges; provisional charges are reserved but not finalized until commit or timeout-based automatic rollback.
3) Truncated or partial fncall outputs are annotated; post-hoc merges (e.g., resumed executions) dedupe by item event_hash so customers are not billed twice for resumed continuations.
4) Reconciliation job (nightly + on-demand) produces deterministic explanations for every charge with links to ledger events, visible in Console cost breakdowns for affected customers.
5) No regression in latency SLOs for standard 1k qps workloads (<= 5% p50 increase).
design_decisions: Event model: append-only compact ledger events emitted to existing event bus (kafka) as small proto records. We will NOT store full payloads in ledger—only hashes and metadata to keep size low.

Charge semantics: provisional reserve on 'execute_start' + final commit on 'execute_commit'. If commit missing after configurable TTL, nightly reconciliation marks as rolled_back and credits refunded.
Deduplication: item-level canonical hash (canonicalized JSON for structured outputs) used to de-duplicate resumed or replayed executions. Hash algorithm: SHA256 hex.

Prefetch handling: mark prefetch events with prefetch=true and credit them to a provisional pool that is refunded when downstream cancel events observed; use weighted refund when partial fanout succeeded.
Backward compatibility: old invoices retained; migration layer translates event ledger to current billing rows until we cutover at release billing-2026.04.
Visibility: expose 'ledger trace' links in Console and API for audit.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable ledger emitting for 5% of non-chat traffic, write events only (no billing change) and verify event integrity; monitor event loss, size, and consumer lag.
Phase 2 (validation): Enable reconciliation consumer in dry-run mode producing proposed adjustments, compare to existing charges for a selected customer cohort.

Phase 3 (soft-commit): Use ledger commit semantics for low-risk endpoints (embeddings-only pipelines) and enable provisional reservations but do not finalize refunds automatically; operations can apply suggested refunds manually.
Phase 4 (cutover): Full commit + automated nightly reconciliation + Console exposure.
qa_test_plan: Unit tests for event canonicalization and SHA256 hash stability across language SDKs.
Integration tests: e2e non-chat API test that simulates prefetch + cancel + resumed execution and asserts single committed charge.
Load test: 10k items/s simulated fanout with synthetic embeddings and rerank steps to verify event throughput and kafka consumer scaling.
Golden reconciliation tests: deterministic fixture set of ledger events -> expected invoice line items.
Chaos test: drop random ledger events in canary and assert reconciliation detects inconsistencies and triggers alerts.
monitoring_signals: Event publish rate (events/sec) and average event size
Kafka topic lag per consumer group
Provisional reservation vs committed charge ratio (should approach 1 after reconciliation)
Number of double-charge anomalies detected by reconciliation
Console usage queries for 'ledger trace' per customer
Nightly reconciliation delta (USD) and affected accounts count
notes: Trade-offs: storing only hashes reduces storage but means deep forensic debugging may require retrieving raw payloads from archival storage (S3) which we plan to link from ledger when available.
We intentionally avoid moving billing decisions into runtime path; provisional reserves are cheap metadata ops. Final commit happens in reconciler to minimize impact on p95 latency.
Edge case: third-party toolcalls with opaque billing (external RPCs) will emit 'external_call' events and reconciliation will rely on observed downstream success/cancel events to decide final charge.
Privacy: no PII saved in ledger; canonicalization strips user content before hashing when request metadata indicates sensitive content.
